outcome: Maternity care use (e.g., midwifery-to-obstetric transfers, home births)
Spending during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period
cohort: The study compared 22,307 pregnancies across six regions that adopted bundled payments in 2017 with 69,496 pregnancies in twenty matched control regions in the Netherlands.
finding: Bundled payments were associated with an 8.9 percent reduction in midwifery-to-obstetric transfers during delivery, a 1.1 percent decline in home births, and a US$121 reduction in spending per pregnancy, with no observed changes in maternal or neonatal health.
mod_finding: Bundled payments were associated with a 1.1 percent decline in home births.
followup_time: N/A (outcomes measured during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period; specific length of postnatal period not mentioned)
